A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same LongVideo-R1 work with readable text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–D. All 17 pages were compared; appendix pages 12–17 have identical text and rendered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, training and tool-use ablations, timing measurements, and qualitative success and failure cases in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, timing measurements and qualitative cases, including the appendix results.

M1.justification: Hierarchical navigation, multimodal tools, Algorithm 1, SFT/GRPO training and rewards are unchanged. Section 5.2 newly attributes the existing GRPO version to Ego-R1 without changing its objective or procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain CG-Bench training data, LVBench, MLVU and Video-MME evaluations, and the same ultra-long video examples. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1–3 and the remaining comparisons. Ego-R1 already appears as a Video-MME comparator in v1; its additional methodological citations introduce no evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Data partitions, model configurations, metrics, subtitle conditions, training budgets and timing procedures are unchanged. Both specify three SFT epochs followed by two RL epochs and retain the same settings in Appendix B.

E4.justification: Tables 4–7 retain the same analyses of SFT data size, location reward, captioning-model scale and tool-use limits. The qualitative cases and distractor failures in Figures 3–9 and Appendices C–D are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain point-estimate reporting without evaluation seed counts, repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–7 and the qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports 50.0% for LongVideo-R1 and 60.7% for its 'new' variant in both PDFs; that variant's results were already present in v1.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5, the hierarchical definitions in Appendix A and the timing derivation in Appendix B.4 are unchanged. The added attribution accompanying GRPO introduces no mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about efficient hierarchical navigation, training data, competitive QA accuracy and the accuracy-efficiency tradeoff.

C2.justification: Interpretations of benchmark performance, sensitivity to misleading segments, dependence on caption quality and the individual-question assumption are retained. Sections 6.2–6.4 and Appendix D add no new explanation or limitation.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 now identifies the GRPO version as the one introduced in Ego-R1, adding limited specificity about the existing optimizer's provenance. Hyperparameters, prompts, hardware, timing details and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges Ego-R1 as a precedent for multi-round tool use in Section 3.3, the source of the GRPO version in Section 5.2, and inspiration for the drawing style of Figures 1–2. The same 66 bibliography entries are retained.

P1.justification: Changes comprise short attribution insertions, a citation-spacing correction and the version/date header update. The section sequence and substantive narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 gain attribution text in their captions. Layout reflow moves Tables 1–3 from page 6 to 7, Tables 4–7 from page 7 to 8, and Figure 3 from page 8 to 7. Table structures and figure content remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Explicit credit to Ego-R1 in Sections 3.3 and 5.2 and Figures 1–2 improves scholarly attribution and clarifies the provenance of existing components. This is a limited improvement: the scientific evidence, conclusions and appendix material remain unchanged, while the layout changes primarily redistribute existing content.
